name: home internet
label: Home internet

modes.title: No connection
modes.symptom: a complete loss of the broadband connection
customer_says: My internet has gone off completely and nothing in the house will connect.
The broadband is dead. The router has a red light on it and none of our devices can get online.
We've got no internet whatsoever. It just dropped and it hasn't come back.
Everything here is offline, the laptops, the telly, the lot. The router keeps flashing but nothing happens.

causes.cause: a failed line card in the local exchange
a fibre cable severed by roadworks
a power failure at the street cabinet
fixes: restoring mains power to the street cabinet
connecting a temporary generator to the street cabinet

workarounds: tether a laptop to a mobile phone hotspot for essential use
collect a loan 4G dongle from the nearest Meridian shop
aftercare: restart the router if the connection has not come back
leave the router switched on for ten minutes so it can reconnect by itself

modes.title: Slow speeds
modes.symptom: download speeds far below the normal level
customer_says: My internet is crawling. Pages take forever to open and videos keep stopping to buffer.
The connection is so slow it's basically unusable. A speed test gave me a tiny fraction of what I pay for.
Everything online has slowed right down. I can't even get a video call to hold together.
We're connected, but it's painfully slow on every device in the house, even right next to the router.

causes.cause: congestion on the regional backhaul link
fixes: moving traffic onto a spare backhaul link

causes.cause: a degraded optical module in the aggregation switch

workarounds: schedule large downloads for after midnight
lower the picture quality setting on streaming devices
aftercare: restart the router once so it picks up the full speed profile
run a speed test from the Meridian portal and report any result that still looks low

modes.title: Connection keeps dropping
modes.symptom: broadband sessions dropping every few minutes
customer_says: My internet keeps cutting out. It works for a few minutes, then drops, then comes back again.
The connection is up and down like a yo-yo. I get thrown out of every video meeting.
The broadband won't stay connected. The light on the router goes orange every couple of minutes.
We keep losing the internet for a minute or so at a time. It has happened dozens of times now.

causes.cause: a faulty amplifier on the local cable segment
an unstable routing table after a core software upgrade
water damage in an underground joint box
fixes: drying out and resealing the underground joint box

workarounds: pause automatic backups and software updates until the line is stable
switch video meetings to audio only to ride out the short drops
aftercare: restart the router once to clear the old session
check that smart-home devices have rejoined the network

modes.title: Websites not loading
modes.symptom: web pages failing to load while the line stays connected
customer_says: The router says I'm connected, but hardly any websites will open. I just get an error page.
My internet looks fine on the router, yet nothing loads in the browser. Some apps work and some don't.
I'm online in theory, but every site I try times out. It is the same on my phone over the Wi-Fi.
Websites won't come up at all. The connection light is green, so I don't understand what is wrong.

causes.cause: a crashed domain name resolver cluster
fixes: restarting the domain name resolver cluster

causes.cause: an expired certificate on the web filtering platform
fixes: renewing the certificate on the web filtering platform
flushing the corrupted address lookup cache

workarounds: enter a public domain name server address in the device's network settings
turn off the family filter from the Meridian portal for the time being
aftercare: close and reopen the browser so it picks up the restored service
switch the family filter back on if it was turned off

wrong_customer_side: a worn-out router in the home
an unpaid bill that has restricted the account
a loose lead at the wall socket
wrong_provider_side: planned maintenance at the local exchange
a nationwide outage at the main data centre
a billing system error that suspended lines by mistake
